key_points: Initial request (CL-01, SH-CS): build an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and fix wrong bills. Investigation found this framing wrong: response times are within SLA (median 1.6d vs 3.0d SLA, E-03), so a response-speed fix (H-FRAMING-RESPONSE-SPEED) was rejected.
Dispute volume doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-04). Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) are ESTIMATED-read and 1785 (59%) are ACTUAL-read (E-01).

The original hypothesis (PD-1@v1) attributed the ESTIMATED-dispute share to a manual-read route-completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-06) and staffing (SH-FIELD claim, E-07), but this was invalidated by E-11: 95% of those bills (1184/1240) actually had an accepted AMI read exported to billing yet rejected by a validation rule, not a missing read.

Revised problem (PD-1@v2): billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 exactly at the surge onset (E-12), compares raw register values against 12-month history with no unit scaling and rejects reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, driving estimate substitution for 1184/1240 ESTIMATED disputes (95%, E-11/E-13/E-14). Tariff change was ruled out (E-02, E-05).
This BV-17 mechanism explains only the 41% ESTIMATED-read share; the cause of the larger 59% ACTUAL-read dispute majority remains unestablished by current evidence.

Release decision: HOLD. Grounds given are a missing actual-read dispute segment analysis (1190 missing records), the critical open obligation VOB-R-6 intersecting the release scope (analyze_actual_read_dispute_cause:DA-BILL, monitor_dispute_volume_trend:DA-TICKET), and failure of the Layer-1 safety/verification predicate.

A work item (W-WI-ACTUAL-READ-SEGMENT) was marked DONE claiming analysis of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills, but the cited evidence (E-13, E-14) only covers the ESTIMATED-read, firmware v4.2 population -- no evidence substantiates ACTUAL-read-specific findings, matching the deterministic Layer-1 FAIL.

Guardrails that were respected: no automated writes to customer bills (K-BILLWRITE, SC-NO-AUTOMATED-BILL-WRITES) and no unconfirmed field-dispatch changes (K-DISPATCH, SC-NO-UNCONFIRMED-DISPATCH-CHAN); neither action was taken.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE Gate for this problem only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before proceeding.

VOB-U-BV17-DEFECT-VALIDITY remains OPEN: it is still unconfirmed whether BV-17's lack of unit scaling is a defect causing false-positive rejections of normal-consumption reads, or an intentionally correct high-consumption filter; the investigation task is blocked pending this.

Even if BV-17 is confirmed defective, the root-cause fix (a billing-config change, SR-BV17-CONFIG-CORRECTION) cannot ship within the contest window, so the estimate-substitution driver for the 1184 affected disputes stays live until that out-of-band change ships.
No automated agent has write authority over customer bills (K-BILLWRITE); any bill correction/adjustment remains explicitly out of scope regardless of findings.

The BV-17 mechanism accounts for the ESTIMATED-read share of disputes (41%) but not the majority ACTUAL-read share (59%); if a repeat analysis again fails to isolate a mechanism for that majority, success criterion SC-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE-BEFORE-REM stays unmet.

Two unknowns remain OPEN: whether a return of dispute volume to baseline is conclusive proof the underlying billing cause is fixed (U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-PROXY / U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDIT), since volume could drop for unrelated reasons.

SH-FIELD's staffing-shortage claim (A-STAFFING-CAUSE-UNCONFIRMED) remains unconfirmed by tool evidence, and the route-completion/staffing pathway is no longer part of the causal mechanism per E-11, so it should not be treated as an established cause.

The dependency review (DR-1) shows the prior problem definition, solution design, several structural remedies, and multiple verification obligations/success criteria tied to PD-1@v1 were invalidated or marked NEEDS_REEVALUATION once E-11 overturned the route-completion premise, so artifacts built on that earlier framing cannot be relied upon.
output.summary: The requester (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and automatically fix wrong bills, framing the Aug-Sep ticket surge (610→1260/month, E-04) as a response-speed problem. Analysis showed response times were already within SLA (E-03), so that framing was rejected. Of 3025 disputed bills, 41% are ESTIMATED-read and 59% ACTUAL-read (E-01). The first hypothesis -- that a manual-read route-completion shortfall (E-06) and reader staffing shortage (E-07, unconfirmed) drove the ESTIMATED-read disputes -- was invalidated when E-11 showed 95% of those bills actually had accepted AMI reads that were rejected by a billing-import rule (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not missing reads. The revised, best-supported explanation (PD-1@v2) is that billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-12), erroneously rejects AMI reads as high-consumption, driving estimate substitution for 1184/1240 (95%) of ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-11, E-13, E-14). This explains only the 41% ESTIMATED-read share; the cause of the 59% ACTUAL-read majority remains unestablished. The release decision is HOLD, not a release: the gate found a missing actual-read dispute-segment analysis (1190 records missing), an open critical verification obligation (VOB-R-6) intersecting the release scope, and a failed Layer-1 safety/verification check -- specifically because a work item claiming to analyze the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills cited evidence (E-13/E-14) that only covers the unrelated ESTIMATED-read, firmware v4.2 population. No bill-write or field-dispatch actions were taken, consistent with the no-automated-bill-writes (K-BILLWRITE) and no-unconfirmed-dispatch (K-DISPATCH) constraints.
